context_purpose: A rider wants reasonable assurance that a stranger driver poses no known violent-offender risk before a late-night shared ride.

norm_violation_today.reason: Full ID and licence photos go to every member of a group chat, far beyond the one rider who needs a safety assurance.

purpose_sufficiency.lost: A clean list result says nothing about people with no record yet, and cannot show the driver is insured, sober or the same person as the licence holder.

transmission_check.reason: The photo request is a group-admin habit with no legal duty, so a proof can replace it; whether police would issue such a non-membership credential is a separate question.

context_purpose: A school bus driver must hand a child only to an adult the guardian has authorised.

norm_violation_today.reason: Writing the aunt's ID number and circulating the parent's phone number is plausibly more than a handover check needs, but this is routine child-safety practice.

purpose_sufficiency.lost: Almost nothing; a one-time pass conveys the authorisation, though it does not itself prove the person presenting it is the aunt.

transmission_check.reason: The school sets handover procedure for child safety and may require a name record; I cannot confirm what regulators require.

context_purpose: A hot-spring hotel directs guests to the correct gendered bath hall and applies its tattoo-age policy.

norm_violation_today.reason: Copying a whole ID card, with number and address, to decide a hall assignment collects far more than the one fact needed.

purpose_sufficiency.lost: Nothing material; the venue needs only a yes/no, though the predicate is odd and the national ID may not carry a gender marker the wallet can attest.

transmission_check.reason: The hotel has no stated legal duty to copy the ID, so a minimal proof is allowed.

context_purpose: A union organiser must confirm that each voter is an eligible dues-paying member of an affiliated union and votes once.

norm_violation_today.reason: Sending employer name and payroll slips to a host union exposes workers' membership and workplace to people with no need to see them.

purpose_sufficiency.lost: Weighting by affiliate and detecting fraud in small affiliates may need the branch, and a tiny anonymity set undermines the hiding.

transmission_check.reason: Voting rules are set by union bylaws and labour law I cannot confirm, and they may require an auditable roll.

context_purpose: A kindergarten receptionist must release a child only to someone the guardian has authorised for that day.

norm_violation_today.reason: Forwarded chat screenshots expose other families' names and phone numbers, which the receptionist has no need to see.

purpose_sufficiency.lost: A delegation proves guardian authorisation but not identity of the presenter, driver trustworthiness or insurance, so staff will likely still check ID.

transmission_check.reason: The duty of care is a school practice and I cannot confirm whether any rule requires an ID check at pickup.

context_purpose: A union election committee must run a valid strike vote limited to eligible members, one vote each.

norm_violation_today.reason: A vendor and staff able to link names to votes break the expected secrecy of a ballot, and crew fear employer exposure.

purpose_sufficiency.lost: Nothing for ballot eligibility, but the committee still needs the roll for a verifiable member count, so only vote-to-name unlinkability is gained.

transmission_check.reason: Strike-vote rules likely require an auditable eligibility roll and count, but I cannot confirm whether an anonymous ballot satisfies them.

context_purpose: A hospital ICU desk must admit only spouses and named proxies during restricted visiting hours.

norm_violation_today.reason: Photocopying visitors' ID cards and logging them keeps full identity records beyond the single admission check.

purpose_sufficiency.lost: A bare list-membership bit cannot confirm the person at the desk is the listed one without an ID or device-bound check, and infection or incident tracing may need a name log.

transmission_check.reason: Hospitals may keep visitor logs for infection control or security, and I cannot confirm what is required.

context_purpose: A concert organiser wants to stop scalped or resold tickets and duplicate entry at the gate.

norm_violation_today.reason: Keeping a persistent face template and ID-linked account long after the show goes beyond what a one-night entry check needs.

purpose_sufficiency.lost: A nullifier stops duplicate entry, but binding the person to the ticket still needs a biometric on the holder's phone, and lending the phone defeats it.

transmission_check.reason: The organiser has no stated legal duty to hold faces, so a template-free scheme is allowed; real-name ticketing rules, if any, are unclear to me.
